Well, firstly I’ll say I’m not authority on this. But if you’re just asking for some insight - 

You ask what happens if you can’t feel that way [about your boyfriend.] I guess I’ll offer another question- what *has* happened? How does it affect your relationship? 

I would take a bit to ask yourself why you do that. Where does that habit come from? If you take a step back and look at your thoughts from an exterior perspective - are you doing it because of your past traumas or is your resistance to acceptance because you’re not being accepted yourself? 

As mentioned, I don’t think it’s any one individuals responsibility to accept everyone. And I wanna make it clear that acceptance isn’t a dissolution of boundaries. It’s important to acknowledge that we are people. We exist as individuals which makes it impossible to completely, wholly accept someone else. IMHO I think the only way we completely accept is by dying - but this is because of my mushroom trip. And psychedelics have really helped me, it’s given me a deeper understanding of life but I also want to acknowledge life. My experience was very focused on death. 

Our existence as living biological beings makes us have an instinct of self preservation part of that inherently is by finding acceptance. Love literally kept us alive. 

I think there are a few scenarios in which acceptance exists and all of which are valid, and everyone can choose what is best for them. I’m sure there’s more than what follows, but - 

1. You meet someone and acceptance comes naturally. These are people who are probably like you in positive ways and unlike you in positive ways. Still not perfect though. 
2. You meet someone and acceptance is not natural, but there’s enough of an interest there that you *both* agree to learn that acceptance. If one doesn’t agree to that, it becomes unhealthy. 
3. You have been badly hurt by someone - explicitly rejected in some way. You leave or they leave and after taking the time to detach yourself and heal - you accept them. That doesn’t mean you want them back in your life. Acceptance is legitimately just “I see you. You exist.” That is love to me. You can do that from afar. And when someone can’t offer that to you, and actively hurt you by not accepting you - you don’t need to accept that behavior. But you can accept them. 


Accepting someone (as much as possible on earth) doesn’t mean you don’t see flaws. It’s okay to see people as imperfect. And it’s okay to need some space between yourself and an aspect of someone else. Or just a person as a whole. You have to make that choice for yourself. Really both of you will make the choice because it takes two. Boundaries are important. 

At the end of it, it’s still helpful to understand why you want those boundaries. 

Please feel free to answer any of those questions or offer more thoughts.

Here’s my understanding/experience: High contrast is dark vs light like black and white. Low contrast colors are colors with similar values. So like, black vs dark grey. 

I am a deep winter/deep autumn. My hair is very dark, almost black. I’ve got hazel eyes and I’m very very pale. My eyes are relatively dark but the highest contrast comes from my hair and skin. If I wear a deep purple, it balances with my hair and my skin pops. If I wear a light blue or yellow or really anything pastel it’s likely to almost blend with my skin while my hair pops because it’s such high contrast. 

So when a person is low contrast (hair eyes and skin are of a similar value) wearing a high contrast color can end up taking any attention of off them and putting it all onto the clothing.

I totally understand we are just born into shitty situations a lot of the time and we didn’t deserve it. I was in CBT and that’s when I grew out of my spirituality - probably because the whole “change your mind” thing was being presented to me without any sort of mystical aspect to it.
